recipes.name: Fond Blanc de Volaille (White Chicken Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: A clear, pale, gently savory stock that tastes of chicken and sweet vegetables without any browned notes.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light stock that carries some protein and gelatin from the bones and minerals from the vegetables, with no added salt so the dish it goes into sets the seasoning.

ingredients.baseName: Chicken, broiler, back, meat and skin

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and halved, one half studded with a clove
a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Rinse the chicken carcasses and wings under cold water and put them in a large pot.
Cover with the cold water and bring slowly to a simmer over medium heat, 20 to 30 minutes, skimming off the grey foam as it rises.
Add the carrot, the onion studded with the clove, the leek, celery, garlic, the bouquet garni of thyme, bay and parsley stalks, the peppercorns and the white wine.
Keep at a bare simmer, never a boil, for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, skimming now and then. Do not salt.
Strain through a fine sieve lined with damp muslin without pressing the solids, cool quickly, and lift off the fat once cold. Keep 2 to 3 days in the fridge or freeze.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the chicken bones and skin, mostly as gelatin.
From the carrot, leek and celery.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Fond blanc de volaille
Guide Michelin, Révision des bases : préparer un fond blanc

recipes.curationNote: Michelin (750 g to 1 kg bones for 1.5 L, clove-studded onion, leek white, bouquet garni) and Meilleur du Chef (1 kg giblets, 1.5 L water, half a glass of white wine, peppercorns, about 1 h 30 simmer) agree. 2.5 L water reduces to about 1.5 L, so 6 servings of 1 cup (250 ml).

recipes.name: Fond Brun de Veau (Brown Veal Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep, roasted and meaty, with the sweetness of browned vegetables and a body that coats the tongue from the bones.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich-tasting but lean stock that brings gelatin from the veal bones and a little potassium from the vegetables, with no salt added.

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Heat the oven to 480°F (250°C). Spread the veal bones in a roasting tin and roast for 15 to 30 minutes, turning once, until well browned.
Add the carrot, onion and garlic to the tin and roast 10 to 15 minutes more, then stir in the tomato paste and give it 3 to 5 minutes.
Tip everything into a stockpot, pour off the fat, and deglaze the tin with a little of the water, scraping the brown bits into the pot.
Add the rest of the cold water and the bouquet garni of thyme, bay and parsley stalks. Bring to a simmer and skim.
Simmer very gently, uncovered, for 5 to 6 hours, skimming and topping up with a little water if the bones show. Do not salt.
Strain through a fine sieve without pressing, cool fast and lift off the fat. Keep up to 48 hours in the fridge, or freeze.

nutritionHighlights.note: Mostly gelatin drawn from the roasted veal bones.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Fond brun de veau
Wikipédia, Demi-glace (fond brun and espagnole in the classic sauce system)

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef gives 1 kg bones, 100 g carrot, 50 g onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp tomato paste, 2 L water for 1 L, roasting at 250°C. 4 servings of 1 cup. Veal bones are not in the database.

recipes.name: Fumet de Poisson (Fish Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, clean and briny, with white wine and shallot sweetness behind the taste of the sea.
recipes.healthBenefit: A quick, lean stock that carries minerals and a little protein from the fish bones, made without salt.

ingredients.name: white fish bones and heads (sole, turbot, whiting), gills removed

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Soak the fish bones and heads in cold water for 10 to 15 minutes to draw out the blood, then drain.
Melt the butter in a wide pan and sweat the carrot, onion, shallot and leek over low heat without colour, 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the bones and stir for 3 to 4 minutes until they turn opaque.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, then add the cold water and the bouquet garni.
Bring to a simmer, skim, and cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, no longer, or the stock turns bitter. Do not salt.
Strain through a fine sieve and cool quickly. Keep 1 to 2 days in the fridge or freeze.

nutritionHighlights.note: Some, from the white fish bones and heads.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Fumet de poisson

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 500 g bones, 300 ml white wine, 50 g carrot, 80 g onion, 30 g shallot, 1 leek, 50 g butter, 600 ml water, 20 to 25 minutes, about 1 L. 4 servings of 1 cup.

recipes.name: Court-Bouillon
recipes.flavorProfile: A fragrant, lightly herbal poaching liquid with the sweetness of carrot and shallot and a dry vermouth lift.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish and shellfish poached in it need no fat, and it is mostly water with a little flavour from the vegetables and herbs.

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Put the water, carrot, shallots, celery, vermouth, thyme, bay, parsley stalks, peppercorns and salt in a wide pan.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes so the vegetables give up their flavour.
Lower the fish or shellfish into the barely trembling liquid and poach 3 to 5 minutes for fillets, longer for a whole fish, without letting it boil.
Strain and keep the liquid if it is wanted for a sauce.
recipes.curationNote: Chef Simon: 600 ml water, 2 carrots, 3 shallots, 100 ml Noilly Prat (optional), thyme, bay, parsley stalks, 2 celery stalks, peppercorns, 10 minutes covered. About 750 ml, 3 servings of 1 cup. Noilly Prat is dry vermouth; the only vermouth row is sweet, so it is listed as not in the database.

recipes.name: Sauce Béchamel
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, creamy and mild, with the soft warmth of nutmeg and a gentle pinch of cayenne.
recipes.healthBenefit: Milk brings calcium and protein; with butter and flour it is a rich sauce best used in measured amounts.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Bring the milk to a boil in one pan.
Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan, add the flour and stir over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes to cook a white roux that does not colour.
Take the roux off the heat and pour on the boiling milk all at once, whisking hard so no lumps form.
Return to the heat and bring to a boil, whisking, then simmer gently for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring the bottom so it does not catch.
Season with salt, cayenne and nutmeg. Press cling film on the surface if it is not used at once.
recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 70 g butter, 70 g flour, 1 L milk, salt, cayenne, nutmeg. About 1 L, 16 servings of 1/4 cup. The white roux is made in the same pan, so it is written in rather than linked to Roux Blond.

components.note: 700 ml, boiling; use Fumet de Poisson for a fish velouté

recipes.name: Sauce Velouté
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky and savory, tasting of the pale stock it is made from, lighter than a béchamel.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made with stock rather than milk, it is lighter than a cream sauce and carries a little protein from the stock.
instructions: Warm the blond roux in a heavy saucepan over low heat.
Pour in the boiling stock a ladle at a time, whisking until smooth after each.
Bring to a boil, whisking, then lower the heat and simmer gently for 20 to 30 minutes, skimming the skin that forms, until it coats a spoon.
Season lightly with salt and white pepper and strain through a fine sieve.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the chicken stock.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 30 g butter, 30 g flour (a blond roux) and 700 ml stock, cooked 30 minutes, for 500 ml. 8 servings of 1/4 cup. Roux Blond makes 8 servings of about 14 g, so 60 g is 4; Fond Blanc makes 6 cups, so 700 ml is about 3.

components.note: 60 g, cooked on to a light brown

recipes.name: Sauce Espagnole
recipes.flavorProfile: Dark, glossy and deeply savory, with roasted veal, smoky salt pork and a round tomato sweetness.
recipes.healthBenefit: A concentrated brown sauce used in small amounts, bringing savory depth for very little fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Brown the lardons in a heavy pan for 4 to 5 minutes, add the carrot and onion and colour them lightly, 5 to 8 minutes.
Pour off the fat, add the white wine and reduce it by half, 2 to 3 minutes.
Cook the roux on low heat until it turns light brown, 3 to 5 minutes, then whisk in the hot brown stock a little at a time.
Add the browned vegetables and lardons, the thyme and bay. Simmer very gently for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours, skimming often.
Strain, return to the pan, add the tomato paste and fresh tomatoes and simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour more, skimming, until reduced to about 500 ml.
Strain once more through a fine sieve. Keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tomatoes and tomato paste.
A little, from the veal stock and lardons.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 1 L brown veal stock, 60 g roux, carrot, onion, 50 g salted lardons, half a glass of white wine, thyme, half a bay leaf, 100 ml tomato concentrate, 3 tomatoes, about 500 ml. The roux is the house Roux Blond taken a little further. 8 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Demi-Glace
recipes.flavorProfile: Intense, glossy and almost sticky, a spoonful of concentrated roasted veal and wine.
recipes.healthBenefit: Used by the spoonful, it adds a great deal of savory depth to a sauce for very little fat.
instructions: Put the espagnole and the brown veal stock in a heavy saucepan and bring to a simmer.
Reduce gently, skimming often, for 45 minutes to 1 hour 15 minutes, until the volume has dropped by more than half and the sauce coats a spoon.
Off the heat, stir in the Madeira if using, then strain through a fine sieve.
Cool and keep 4 to 5 days in the fridge, or freeze in small portions.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, mostly gelatin from the veal stock.

recipes.curationNote: Wikipédia gives the classic Escoffier route: equal parts espagnole and fond brun reduced by more than half until nappant, finished with Madeira. Meilleur du Chef describes the same reduction by half. 500 ml in gives about 240 ml, 8 servings of 2 tbsp (30 ml). Espagnole serving is 1/4 cup, so 250 ml is 4; fond brun 1 cup, so 1.

recipes.name: Sauce Tomate (French Tomato Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: A smooth, savory tomato sauce rounded with salt pork and slowly cooked vegetables, deeper and less sharp than a quick tomato sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tomato paste and slow cooking bring lycopene, and the carrots add vitamin A.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
Melt the butter in a flameproof casserole and brown the diced pork belly for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the carrot, onion and garlic and colour lightly, 5 to 8 minutes. Sprinkle on the flour and stir for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the hot water, the bouquet garni, salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar. Bring to a boil.
Cover and cook in the oven for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the vegetables, and check the seasoning.
recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef, the classic sauce tomate with salt pork and roux: 200 ml concentrate, 50 g butter, 150 g salted pork belly, 160 g carrot, 160 g onion, 4 garlic cloves, 50 g flour, bouquet garni, 1.5 L water, oven 150°C. About 1 L, 8 servings of 1/2 cup.

components.note: about 240 g, warm, from 300 g butter

recipes.name: Sauce Hollandaise
recipes.flavorProfile: Warm, buttery and airy, with a bright edge of lemon and a faint heat from the piment.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich butter and egg sauce, a treat, though the yolks bring vitamin A and choline.
instructions: Whisk the yolks with the cold water in a heavy saucepan or a bowl set over barely simmering water.
Keep whisking over gentle heat until the mixture is pale, thick and foamy and reaches 149°F (65°C), 5 to 8 minutes. Do not let it go hotter or the yolks scramble.
Off the heat, pour in the warm clarified butter in a thin stream, whisking all the time, until thick and glossy.
Season with the lemon juice, salt and a pinch of piment d'Espelette. Keep warm, not hot, over a bain-marie and use within 1 hour.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg yolks and butter.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 300 g clarified butter, 5 yolks, 1 tbsp water per yolk, juice of half a lemon, salt, Espelette, sabayon to 65°C. About 360 ml, 12 servings of 2 tbsp. Beurre Clarifié makes 30 tbsp-servings of about 13 g from 500 g, so 300 g butter clarified is 18.

components.note: about 240 g, warm, from 300 g butter

recipes.name: Sauce Béarnaise
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich and buttery like a hollandaise, sharpened with a shallot and vinegar reduction and fresh tarragon.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich sauce for a steak or fish, a treat in small amounts; the yolks bring vitamin A and choline.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 2 tbsp chopped, half for the reduction, half to finish

instructions: Put the vinegar, shallots, crushed peppercorns and half the tarragon in a small heavy pan and reduce over low heat to about a quarter, 5 to 8 minutes. Let it cool a little.
Add the yolks and the cold water and whisk over very gentle heat until thick and foamy and at 149°F (65°C), 5 to 8 minutes.
Off the heat, whisk in the warm clarified butter in a thin stream until thick.
Strain if you like a smooth sauce, then stir in the rest of the tarragon and the chervil and season with salt and cayenne. Keep warm in a bain-marie and use within 1 hour.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg yolks and butter.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 300 g clarified butter, 5 yolks, 100 ml vinegar, 50 g shallots, 5 g crushed pepper, 2 tbsp tarragon, chervil, salt, cayenne, reduced to a quarter, sabayon to 65°C. About 12 servings of 2 tbsp.

recipes.name: Beurre Blanc
recipes.flavorProfile: Pale, creamy and tangy, a warm emulsion of butter with sharp shallot, white wine and lemon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Almost all butter, so it is a rich sauce for fish served by the spoonful.
instructions: Put the shallot, white wine and lemon juice in a small heavy pan and reduce over medium heat until almost dry, 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the cold water and lower the heat to the minimum.
Whisk in the cold butter a few cubes at a time, adding more only as each melts into a creamy sauce. Never let it boil.
Season with salt and pepper, strain if you want it smooth, and keep warm over a bain-marie for up to 30 minutes.
recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 80 g cold butter, juice of 1 lemon (reviewers find half enough, kept at 20 ml), 70 ml white wine, 1 shallot, 2 to 3 tbsp cold water. About 120 ml, 4 servings of 2 tbsp.

recipes.name: Sauce Mornay
recipes.flavorProfile: A creamy béchamel turned nutty and savory with melted Gruyère, enriched with an egg yolk.
recipes.healthBenefit: Milk and Gruyère bring calcium and protein; it is a rich sauce for gratins.
instructions: Bring the béchamel back to a simmer, whisking.
Off the heat, whisk in the egg yolk, then the grated Gruyère until melted and smooth.
Season with salt, pepper and a little nutmeg. Use at once to coat a gratin, or press cling film on the surface to keep it warm for up to 30 minutes.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the milk, cheese and yolk.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef builds it on a béchamel of 40 g butter, 40 g flour, 500 ml milk, then 50 g Gruyère or Emmental and 1 yolk. Linked to the house béchamel (16 servings per litre, so 500 ml is 8). About 550 ml, 9 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Pâte Brisée (Shortcrust)
recipes.flavorProfile: A crisp, buttery, lightly salted crust that snaps cleanly and stays neutral enough for a savory or a sweet filling.
recipes.healthBenefit: A pastry made from flour and butter, so it is energy dense and best thought of as the shell that carries a filling rather than a food in itself.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Put the flour and salt in a bowl, add the cold butter cubes and rub them in with your fingertips for 2 to 3 minutes until the mix looks like coarse sand.
Make a well, add the beaten egg and most of the cold water, and bring it together with a scraper, adding the rest of the water only if it stays dry.
Press the dough into a ball without kneading, flatten it into a disc, wrap it and chill for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Roll it out 3 to 4 mm thick on a floured surface, line a 9 to 10 inch (24 to 26 cm) tart tin without stretching the dough, prick the base and chill again for 20 to 30 minutes.
To blind bake, line with parchment and dried beans and bake at 350°F to 400°F (180°C to 200°C) for 15 to 20 minutes, then remove the beans and bake 5 to 10 minutes more until pale gold.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the butter, which is what makes the crust short.

citations.source: Wikilivres, Livre de cuisine : Pâte brisée

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 200 g flour, 100 g butter, 1 egg, 50 to 65 g water, salt, about 400 g of dough. Wikilivres: 250 g flour, 125 g butter, optional egg, a little water, salt, blind bake at 200°C. Same 2:1 ratio. One 24 to 26 cm crust cut in 8.

recipes.name: Pâte Sucrée (Sweet Tart Pastry)
recipes.flavorProfile: A sweet, fine, biscuit-like crust that melts a little on the tongue and tastes of butter and vanilla.
recipes.healthBenefit: A sweet pastry rich in butter and sugar, so it belongs to the treat end of a meal.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Beat the soft butter with the icing sugar and salt for 1 to 2 minutes until smooth, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Add the flour all at once and mix only until the dough comes together, without working it.
Flatten into a disc, wrap and chill for at least 1 hour, or up to 2 days.
Roll it 3 mm thick between two sheets of parchment, line a 9 to 10 inch (24 to 26 cm) tart ring and chill 20 to 30 minutes.
Blind bake at 325°F to 340°F (160°C to 170°C) for 10 to 15 minutes for a part-baked case, or 20 to 25 minutes for a fully baked one, until evenly golden.

citations.source: Wikilivres, Livre de cuisine : Pâte brisée (sweet version)

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef pâte sucrée: 200 g flour, 100 g butter, 80 g icing sugar, salt, 1 egg, vanilla, creamed method, blind bake 170°C 10 to 15 min. Wikilivres sweet version adds 100 g powdered sugar to 250 g flour and 125 g butter. The database has no icing sugar row, so granulated cane sugar is listed with cutPrep icing sugar: it is the same sucrose, ground fine.

recipes.name: Pâte Feuilletée (Puff Pastry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hundreds of thin, crackling, buttery layers that shatter when bitten and puff high in the oven.
recipes.healthBenefit: Made of flour, water and a great deal of butter, so it is rich and energy dense and a small portion goes a long way.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: cold, for the beurre de tourage

instructions: Mix the flour, salt and cold water into a smooth dough (the détrempe), shape it into a ball, cut a cross in the top, wrap and chill for 1 to 2 hours.
Beat the cold butter between two sheets of parchment into a flat square about 1/2 inch (1 cm) thick that is as supple as the dough.
Roll the dough into a cross shape, set the butter square in the middle and fold the four flaps over it to enclose it completely.
Roll the block into a long rectangle, fold it in three like a letter and turn it a quarter turn: that is one turn. Give a second turn, then chill for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Repeat until you have given six turns in all, two at a time with a rest in the fridge between each pair. Chill at least 1 hour before rolling and baking at 400°F to 430°F (200°C to 220°C).

nutritionHighlights.note: From the large share of butter folded through the layers.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 500 g flour, 250 g water, 10 g salt, 375 g butter, about 1.1 kg, six turns. Wikipédia confirms détrempe plus beurre de tourage and the classic six turns. 20 servings of about 55 g.

recipes.name: Pâte à Choux
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, hollow, crisp-shelled puffs with a soft, eggy inside that take any sweet or savory filling.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly egg and flour, so each small puff brings a little protein along with the butter.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D
Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Bring the milk, water, butter and salt to a full boil in a saucepan so the butter melts completely.
Take the pan off the heat, tip in all the flour at once and beat hard with a wooden spoon until smooth.
Put the pan back over medium heat and stir for 2 to 4 minutes to dry the paste, until it pulls away from the sides and leaves a thin film on the base.
Move the paste to a bowl, let it cool for 3 to 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs a little at a time until the dough is glossy and falls from the spoon in a thick ribbon.
Pipe small mounds on a lined tray and bake at 340°F to 360°F (170°C to 180°C) for 25 to 35 minutes without opening the oven, until puffed, golden and light.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Pâte à choux

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 125 g milk, 125 g water, 165 g flour, 100 g butter, salt, 250 g eggs, 170°C 25 to 35 min. Wikipédia gives the 1-2-4-8-16 rule (1 L liquid, 20 g salt, 400 g butter, 800 g flour, 16 eggs), dry the panade 4 to 5 min, 180°C, never open the oven. Proportions agree. 250 g eggs is 5 large eggs. About 40 small choux.

recipes.name: Pâte à Crêpes (Crêpe Batter)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin, tender, lacy-edged pancakes that taste of egg, milk and browned butter.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light batter of milk, egg and flour that brings some protein and calcium, and stays modest when filled simply.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Put the flour, salt and sugar in a bowl, make a well, add the eggs and whisk from the middle outward to a thick, smooth paste.
Whisk in the cold milk a little at a time to keep it free of lumps, then the water, the melted butter and the rum.
Cover and rest the batter in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Heat a lightly buttered crêpe pan over medium high heat, pour in a small ladle of batter and swirl it thin over the base.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes until the edges lift and the underside is golden, flip and cook 30 seconds to 1 minute more. Stack under a cloth.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Pâte à crêpes

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 125 g flour T55, 30 g melted butter, salt, optional sugar, 3 eggs, 300 ml cold milk, 2 tbsp water, 2 tsp dark rum or orange-flower water, rest 1 h, about 12 crêpes. Wikipédia confirms flour, eggs, milk and water, sugar for the sweet kind, a smooth batter and optional rest. The rum is optional; orange-flower water is not in the database so the rum was kept.

recipes.name: Crème Pâtissière (Pastry Cream)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, smooth, vanilla custard that holds its shape and tastes of egg yolk and warm milk.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein and calcium from the milk and eggs, along with a fair amount of sugar, so it is a filling for treats.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D
Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Bring the milk to a simmer with the split vanilla pod and its seeds, then take it off the heat and leave it to infuse for 10 to 15 minutes.
Whisk the yolks, whole eggs and sugar in a bowl for 1 to 2 minutes until pale, then whisk in the flour.
Lift out the vanilla pod and pour half of the hot milk onto the egg mixture, whisking, then pour it all back into the pan.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the base, until it thickens and bubbles, then keep cooking and whisking for 4 to 5 minutes more so the flour loses its raw taste.
Pour into a shallow dish, press plastic film onto the surface, cool quickly and chill for at least 2 hours. Keep 2 to 3 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg yolks, eggs and milk.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 1 L milk, 250 g sugar, 100 g flour T55, 6 yolks, 2 eggs, 1 vanilla pod, cook 4 to 5 min after thickening. Wikipédia agrees on milk, yolks or eggs, sugar, flour or starch, vanilla infusion and covering the surface. About 1.1 kg, 16 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Crème Anglaise
recipes.flavorProfile: A pourable, silky vanilla custard sauce, sweet and eggy, served cold over cakes, fruit and îles flottantes.
recipes.healthBenefit: Brings protein from the yolks and calcium from the milk with added sugar, so a spoonful is a treat rather than a staple.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Bring the milk to a simmer with the split vanilla pod and its seeds, then take it off the heat and infuse for 10 to 15 minutes.
Whisk the yolks and sugar for 1 to 2 minutes until pale, then pour on the hot milk a little at a time, whisking.
Return to the pan over low heat and stir constantly with a wooden spoon in a figure of eight, without letting it boil, for 5 to 10 minutes.
Stop when it reaches 180°F to 183°F (82°C to 84°C) and coats the spoon so that a finger drawn across it leaves a clean line (à la nappe).
Strain at once into a cold bowl, stir now and then as it cools, then chill for at least 2 hours. Keep 1 to 2 days in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg yolks and milk.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 1 L milk, 8 to 10 yolks, 150 g sugar, 1 vanilla pod, cook to 82°C à la nappe and strain. Wikipédia: milk, fresh yolks, sugar, vanilla, cook between 82 and 84°C or it turns lumpy. 9 yolks is the middle of the range. 16 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Roux Blond
recipes.flavorProfile: A pale golden paste of butter and flour that smells of toasted hazelnut and thickens a sauce without tasting of raw flour.
recipes.healthBenefit: Only butter and flour, so it adds a little energy to the sauce it thickens and nothing more.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over low to medium heat until it foams.
Add the flour all at once and stir with a wooden spoon or whisk into a smooth paste.
Keep stirring over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until the roux turns a light straw gold and smells of hazelnut; stop at 1 to 2 minutes for a roux blanc, or carry on 8 to 10 minutes for a roux brun.
Use it at once, whisking in cold or warm liquid gradually, or cool it and keep it covered in the fridge for up to 1 week.

citations.source: Croq-Kilos, Comment faire un roux en cuisine

recipes.curationNote: Croq-Kilos: equal weights butter and flour, blanc 1 to 2 min, blond 3 to 5 min, brun 8 to 10 min. Wikipédia: three roux by cooking time, blond with a hazelnut taste, Curnonsky 80 g butter to 75 g flour per litre. 120 g of roux in 8 servings of 1 tbsp (about 15 g); velouté and espagnole in this file use 4 servings for 1 L.

recipes.name: Duxelles
recipes.flavorProfile: A dark, dry, intensely savory hash of mushrooms and shallot, earthy and buttery, used to stuff, spread and flavor.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly mushrooms, which bring B vitamins, potassium and some fiber, cooked in a modest amount of butter.
instructions: Squeeze the chopped mushrooms in a clean cloth, a handful at a time, to press out as much liquid as you can, and toss them with the lemon juice.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the shallot and onion for 3 to 5 minutes without browning.
Add the mushrooms, turn the heat up and cook uncovered, stirring often, for 10 to 15 minutes, until all the moisture has gone and the mixture is dry and starting to stick.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg, stir in the parsley and take off the heat.
Cool and keep covered in the fridge for 3 to 4 days, or freeze in small portions.

nutritionHighlights.note: Riboflavin and niacin from the mushrooms.

citations.source: Aftouch Cuisine, La duxelles de champignons

recipes.curationNote: Wikipédia gives Escoffier: 250 g mushrooms pressed, onion and shallot, butter and oil, parsley, stewed dry. Aftouch: 500 g button mushrooms, 2 onions, 2 shallots, 50 g butter, salt, pepper, nutmeg, high heat 6 to 7 min until dry, then 100 ml cream. Kept the classic dry duxelles without cream, since it is a base; a cook can add cream for a stuffing. About 360 ml, 6 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Beurre Clarifié (Clarified Butter)
recipes.flavorProfile: Clear, golden, pure-tasting butter fat that can take high heat without burning and gives a clean butter flavor.
recipes.healthBenefit: Almost all fat once the milk solids and water are gone, so it is used in small amounts; removing the solids also takes out most of the lactose and casein.
instructions: Melt the butter in a small heavy saucepan over very low heat, without stirring, for 10 to 15 minutes.
Skim off the white foam that rises to the top with a spoon.
Pour the clear yellow butter off slowly into a jar, leaving the milky whey at the bottom of the pan behind, or strain it through muslin.
Keep covered in the fridge for up to 1 month.

nutritionHighlights.note: Nearly all of it, mostly saturated, from the butter.

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: melt over very low heat without stirring, skim the foam, pour off the clear butter leaving the whey; 100 g butter gives 80 to 85 g. Wikipédia: melted then decanted to remove casein and whey. 500 g butter gives about 400 g, 30 tbsp of about 13 g; hollandaise and béarnaise here each use 18.

recipes.name: Beurre Maître d'Hôtel
recipes.flavorProfile: Cold butter flecked green with parsley and sharpened with lemon, melting into a glossy, fresh sauce on a hot steak or fish.
recipes.healthBenefit: A butter for melting over food in thin slices; the parsley adds a little vitamin K and C.
instructions: Beat the soft butter with a fork or spatula until creamy, like a paste.
Work in the parsley, lemon juice, salt and pepper until evenly mixed.
Spoon it onto parchment or plastic film, roll it into a log about 1 1/4 inches (3 cm) across and twist the ends.
Chill for at least 1 to 2 hours until firm, then cut in slices to set on hot grilled meat or fish. Keeps 1 week in the fridge or 2 months frozen.

citations.source: Meilleur du Chef, Beurre maître d'hôtel

recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 100 g soft butter, 15 g chopped parsley, a squeeze of lemon, salt, pepper, rolled and chilled, about 120 g. Wikipédia gives Escoffier (250 g butter, a spoonful of parsley, 8 g salt, 1 g pepper, 5 or 6 drops of lemon) and Nignon. 8 slices of about 15 g.

recipes.name: Persillade
recipes.flavorProfile: A bright green, sharp mix of raw garlic and parsley that wakes up anything it is scattered over at the last minute.
recipes.healthBenefit: Parsley brings vitamin K, vitamin C and folate, and the garlic brings its sulfur compounds, in small, flavorful amounts.

ingredients.cutPrep: flat leaf, leaves only, very finely chopped

instructions: Chop the parsley leaves and the garlic together on a board with a large knife until very fine.
Stir in the olive oil and season lightly with salt and pepper; leave out the oil when it is to be tossed into a hot pan at the end of cooking.
Scatter it over potatoes, mushrooms, fish, snails or grilled meat in the last 1 to 2 minutes of cooking or just before serving.
Keep covered in the fridge for 3 to 5 days.
recipes.curationNote: Wikipédia: parsley and garlic chopped together, sometimes shallot, olive oil, vinegar or breadcrumbs. Croq-Kilos: about 30 g flat parsley, 3 to 4 garlic cloves, 3 to 4 tbsp olive oil, optional lemon, keeps 3 to 5 days. Oil reduced to 2 tbsp so it stays a chopped seasoning. About 8 tbsp.

recipes.name: Mayonnaise
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, glossy, pale yellow emulsion, rich and gently tangy with mustard and vinegar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly oil, so it is energy dense; made with sunflower oil it carries vitamin E and unsaturated fat.
instructions: Have every ingredient at room temperature. Whisk the yolks, mustard, salt and pepper in a bowl for 30 seconds.
Add the oil drop by drop at first, whisking constantly, until the sauce starts to thicken.
Once it has taken, pour the rest of the oil in a thin stream, still whisking, until thick and glossy.
Whisk in the vinegar at the end to loosen and sharpen it, then taste for salt.
Keep covered in the fridge and use within 24 hours, since the yolks are raw.
recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 2 yolks, 1 glass of oil, 1 tsp mustard, 1 tbsp vinegar optional, salt, white pepper, keeps 24 h at 4°C, about 20 cl. Wikipédia: yolks, vinegar, oil, salt, pepper, mustard or lemon, oil added gradually. Neutral sunflower oil, as French home cooks use. Dijon is listed as the strong (hot) mustard row; white pepper is not in the database. About 240 ml, 16 tbsp.

recipes.name: Aïoli
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, golden garlic emulsion with the fruitiness of olive oil and a raw garlic heat that builds as you eat.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly olive oil, which brings monounsaturated fat, with garlic; it is rich, so a spoonful beside vegetables and fish is the way it is eaten.
instructions: Pound the garlic with the salt in a mortar for 2 to 3 minutes until it is a smooth, sticky paste.
Work in the egg yolks with the pestle until combined.
Add the olive oil a few drops at a time, turning the pestle steadily in one direction, then in a thin stream once the sauce has taken, until thick enough to hold the pestle upright.
Finish with the lemon juice and pepper, taste for salt, and serve within the day with poached cod, boiled vegetables and eggs for le grand aïoli.
recipes.curationNote: Wikipédia: originally only garlic and olive oil pounded in a mortar; egg yolk, lemon, bread or potato are common additions. Meilleur du Chef: 2 yolks, half a lemon, 6 garlic cloves, 1 glass of oil, salt, pepper, Espelette, notes the Provence version with olive oil. Kept the yolk, which most Provençal home cooks now use because the pure garlic and oil emulsion breaks easily; the mortar is kept. About 16 tbsp.

recipes.name: Vinaigrette à la Moutarde
recipes.flavorProfile: A sharp, mustardy, lightly creamy dressing that clings to green leaves and cuts through rich food.
recipes.healthBenefit: A dressing of olive oil and vinegar that brings monounsaturated fat and helps the fat-soluble vitamins in a salad be absorbed.
instructions: Whisk the mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper in a bowl until the salt dissolves, about 30 seconds.
Whisk in the olive oil in a thin stream until the dressing thickens and emulsifies.
Taste on a leaf and adjust the salt or vinegar, then dress the salad just before serving. Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 1 week; whisk again before use.
recipes.curationNote: Meilleur du Chef: 2 tbsp oil to 1 tbsp vinegar, salt. Wikipédia: generally one third vinegar to two thirds oil, a spoonful of mustard optional. Kept the 1 to 2 ratio and a full spoon of Dijon for the moutarde version. About 9 tbsp.

recipes.name: Crème Fraîche Maison
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, spoonable, softly tangy cream with a nutty richness that does not split when it is boiled into a sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: A cultured cream that brings live lactic bacteria when eaten uncooked, along with a good deal of saturated fat, so it is used by the spoonful.
instructions: Pour the cream into a clean glass jar and stir in the cultured buttermilk.
Cover loosely with a cloth or a lid set on without screwing, and leave at warm room temperature, about 72°F (22°C), for 12 to 24 hours, until it has thickened and tastes pleasantly sour.
Stir, close the jar and chill for at least 4 to 6 hours, during which it thickens further.
Keep in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, and keep 2 tbsp back to start the next batch.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the lactic bacteria in the buttermilk, when eaten uncooked.

citations.source: Cuisine Culinaire, Crème fraîche épaisse maison

recipes.curationNote: Cuisine Culinaire: 240 ml heavy cream, 1 tbsp cultured buttermilk, 12 h or more at about 22°C, then fridge, up to 2 weeks. Wikipédia: thick crème fraîche is cream seeded with lactic cultures and matured. Doubled the batch. About 510 ml, 16 servings of 2 tbsp.

recipes.name: Croûtons
recipes.flavorProfile: Golden, crunchy cubes of day-old bread, buttery and lightly salted, that soak up soup without falling apart at once.
recipes.healthBenefit: A way to use up stale bread that adds crunch and some carbohydrate; toasting in butter makes them richer than plain bread.

ingredients.cutPrep: day-old, cut in 3/4 inch (2 cm) cubes or slices

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). For slices to float on soup, rub each slice with the cut garlic first.
Toss the bread with the melted butter and salt on a baking tray in one layer.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp; or brown them in a frying pan over medium heat for 5 to 8 minutes, turning often.
Cool on the tray and keep in an airtight tin for 3 to 4 days.
recipes.curationNote: Croq-Kilos: day-old bread cubed, olive oil or melted butter, optional garlic and herbs, oven 180°C 10 to 15 min turning halfway, or pan. Wikipédia: dry bread browned in butter, fried in oil or dried in the oven, served with onion soup and bouillabaisse. Butter chosen as the French soup croûton. 4 servings of 1/2 cup.

recipes.name: Oignons Confits (Slow-Cooked Onions)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, jammy, deep golden onions, sweet and sour from the slow cooking and a little balsamic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly onion, which brings fiber and quercetin, with added sugar that makes it a condiment to eat by the spoonful.

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni

instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pan over low heat, add the onions and a pinch of salt, cover and sweat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Uncover and cook over medium low heat for 20 to 25 minutes more, stirring often, until golden.
Stir in the sugar for 3 to 5 minutes, then add the balsamic vinegar, thyme and bay.
Simmer gently for 15 to 25 minutes until syrupy and jam-like, then remove the herbs and season.
Cool, spoon into a clean jar and keep in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
recipes.curationNote: Demotivateur: 500 g sweet onions, 1 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp balsamic, sweat then caramelise then simmer to confit, slow covered version 1 h to 1 h 30. Croq-Kilos: 500 g onions, 100 g sugar, 100 ml balsamic, olive oil, bay, thyme, about 1 h. Kept the lower sugar and the butter, with the thyme and bay. About 250 g, 8 servings of 2 tbsp.

recipes.name: Pâté de Campagne
recipes.flavorProfile: A coarse, meaty country terrine, peppery and rich with liver and a breath of armagnac, cut in thick cool slices.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork liver makes it a dense source of iron, vitamin A and vitamin B12, though it is a rich, salty charcuterie best eaten a slice at a time.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

ingredients.name: quatre-épices (pepper, nutmeg, clove and ginger blend)

ingredients.cutPrep: thin slices, to line the terrine

instructions: Cut the pork belly, liver and back fat into pieces and pass the belly and liver through the coarse plate of a meat grinder (or chop by hand); keep the fat in small cubes.
In a large bowl mix the meats and fat with the onion, garlic, parsley, eggs, crème fraîche, white wine and armagnac.
Season with the salt (about 15 g per kilo of meat), pepper and quatre-épices, mix well with your hands, cover and leave in the fridge for 12 to 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 320°F (160°C). Line a 1.5 to 2 liter terrine with the bacon slices, pack in the mixture, fold the bacon over and lay the bay leaves on top.
Cover, set the terrine in a roasting tin and pour in hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours 15 minutes, until the juices run clear and the center reaches 160°F to 165°F (70°C to 74°C).
Leave to cool, then press it lightly under a weight and keep it in the fridge for 2 to 3 days before slicing, so the flavors settle.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork belly and liver.

citations.source: Dubocalalassiette, Recette du Pâté de Campagne à l'Ancienne

recipes.curationNote: Dubocalalassiette: belly, pork liver, back fat, garlic, onion, parsley, eggs, crème fraîche, white wine, armagnac, 15 g salt and 5 g pepper per kilo, quatre-épices, lined with bacon and bay, bain-marie at 160°C, rest 48 h. Le Parfait: throat and belly with liver, egg, shallot, cognac or armagnac, quatre-épices. Kept the Dubocalalassiette version at a 1.5 kg batch. Armagnac is read through the brandy row. Caul fat omitted.

recipes.name: Rillettes de Porc
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, silky shreds of pork slowly cooked in their fat, salty and peppery, spread thick on bread.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein, B vitamins and zinc, but rillettes are mostly fat by design, so they are a rich spread for small amounts.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål
ingredients.cutPrep: rind removed, cut in 5 cm (2 inch) pieces

instructions: Melt the lard in a heavy cast iron pot over low heat and add the shoulder and belly pieces.
Let them color lightly on all sides for 10 to 15 minutes, turning them.

Add the water, garlic, bay, thyme, salt and pepper, cover and cook on the lowest possible heat (or in the oven at 250°F, 120°C) for 4 to 6 hours, stirring now and then, until the meat falls apart at a touch.
Lift out the herbs, then shred the meat with two forks in the pot, stirring it into the melted fat until it holds together.
Taste for salt and pepper, pack into jars and pour a little of the fat over the top to seal.
Cool and keep in the fridge for at least a day before eating, cold, on toasted bread.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork shoulder and belly.
From the belly and lard, which carry most of the energy.

citations.source: Croq-Kilos, Recette de rillettes de porc

recipes.curationNote: Le Parfait (Le Mans): belly, shoulder and palette with bardière fat and panne, a glass of water, about 6 h on very low heat, crushed; commenters suggest 12 to 15 g salt per kilo. Croq-Kilos: 1.5 kg shoulder, 300 g fatty belly, 25 cl water, garlic, bay, thyme, coarse salt, about 4 h, saindoux optional. Kept a 1.5 kg batch with lard in place of the separate leaf fat.

recipes.name: Mousse de Foies de Volaille
recipes.flavorProfile: A smooth, buttery chicken liver mousse with sweet port and shallot, a hint of orange, under a cap of melted butter.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken liver is one of the richest food sources of vitamin A, folate, iron and vitamin B12; with this much butter it is a rich spread for a little at a time.

ingredients.cutPrep: trimmed of sinews and any green spots
100 g for cooking, 100 g melted for the top

ingredients.name: orange zest
ingredients.cutPrep: zest of half an unwaxed orange

instructions: Melt 100 g of the butter in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the shallot, garlic, bay and thyme with a pinch of salt for 8 to 10 minutes without browning.
Add the livers and cook for 4 to 6 minutes, turning, until browned outside and still pink in the middle.
Pour in the port and let it bubble until reduced by half, 2 to 3 minutes. Off the heat stir in the orange zest and the crushed peppercorns.
Remove the bay and thyme stems and blend everything until very smooth, then press it through a fine sieve for a silky mousse. Taste for salt.
Spoon into ramekins or a small terrine and smooth the top.
Melt the remaining butter gently, pour it over, scatter with chives and chill for 4 to 12 hours until firm.

citations.source: Dubocalalassiette, Pâté de Foie de Volaille au Porto
Elle, Mousse de foies de volaille au Porto

recipes.curationNote: Dubocalalassiette: 400 g livers, 200 g butter (half cooked, half on top), 100 ml port, shallots, garlic, bay, thyme, orange zest, peppercorns, sieved, chives. Elle: 500 g livers poached in white wine, 200 g butter, nutmeg, port, 12 h rest. Followed Dubocalalassiette, with the pink centre and the rest in the fridge from both.

recipes.name: Tapenade
recipes.flavorProfile: A dark, salty Provençal paste of black olives, capers and anchovy, sharp with lemon and soft with olive oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Olives and olive oil bring mostly monounsaturated fat and some vitamin E, and the anchovy adds a little omega-3; it is salty, so a spoonful goes a long way.
instructions: Put the olives, capers, anchovies and garlic in a mortar (or a food processor).
Pound or pulse them to a coarse paste, then add the lemon juice and thyme.
Work in the olive oil a little at a time until the tapenade is thick and spreadable. Season with pepper; it needs no salt.
Let it rest for 1 hour before serving with toasted bread or raw vegetables. It keeps 1 week in the fridge under a film of oil.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the olives and olive oil.
From the olives and olive oil.
From the olives, capers and anchovy.

recipes.curationNote: Marseille Tourisme: 200 g pitted black olives, 2 tbsp capers, 4 anchovy fillets, 1 garlic clove, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 3 tbsp olive oil, pepper, 1 h rest; named after tapena (caper), Marseille around 1880, made in a mortar. Provenceweb: 200 to 300 g olives, 2 to 8 anchovies, capers, garlic, 100 ml olive oil, optional thyme. Followed Marseille Tourisme with oil between the two.

components.note: the whole batch, freshly made and still warm

recipes.name: Gougères
recipes.flavorProfile: Light, hollow cheese puffs with a crisp golden shell and a nutty, salty, eggy middle.
recipes.healthBenefit: The cheese and eggs bring protein and calcium; they are buttery pastry, so a few with a drink is the idea.

ingredients.name: Comté cheese
ingredients.cutPrep: finely grated, 90 g in the dough and 30 g on top

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line two trays with baking paper.
Make the choux paste and, while it is still warm, beat in 90 g of the grated Comté, the nutmeg and pepper.
Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds 3 to 4 cm (1.5 inches) apart, brush with beaten egg and scatter with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 5 minutes, then lower the oven to 350°F (180°C) and bake for 20 to 25 minutes more, without opening the door, until puffed, deep golden and light.
Serve warm, the Burgundian way, with a glass of chilled white wine.

citations.source: France.fr, Recette des gougères au comté
culture: the word on cheese, Gougères

recipes.curationNote: France.fr: 100 g Comté, 25 cl water, 120 g butter, 125 g flour, 4 eggs, bake 160°C 20 to 30 min. culture: 3.5 oz Comté, 3 eggs, 425°F 5 min then 350°F 25 min. The choux base (milk and water, 5 eggs) covers the paste; the extra cheese, nutmeg and glaze are added here. Comté is not in the food database.

recipes.name: Œufs Mimosa
recipes.flavorProfile: Cool hard-boiled egg halves filled with mayonnaise and topped with a fine snow of sieved yolk and chives.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs bring protein, choline, vitamin B12 and vitamin D; the mayonnaise makes them richer, so two or three halves make a starter.
instructions: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 9 to 10 minutes, then cool them at once in cold water.
Peel the eggs, halve them lengthwise and lift out the yolks.
Press the yolks through a fine sieve to make a fine powder: the mimosa.
Mix half the sieved yolk with the mayonnaise, season, and spoon it into the whites.
Scatter the rest of the yolk generously over the top with the chives and parsley, and serve on lettuce leaves. Eat within 24 hours, since the mayonnaise is made with raw yolk.

citations.source: Le Fooding, Œufs mimosa de Faggio Salumeria

recipes.curationNote: Le Fooding: 6 eggs boiled 9 min, mayonnaise from 3 yolks, mustard, wine vinegar and sunflower oil, yolks pressed through a chinois into a fine mimosa, chives. Jardiner Malin: 4 eggs 10 min, mayonnaise mixed with half the yolk, the rest crumbled on top, lettuce, parsley, optional paprika. Mayonnaise points at the base.

recipes.name: Escargots à la Bourguignonne
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender snails baked in their shells under bubbling garlic and parsley butter, eaten with bread to mop it up.
recipes.healthBenefit: Snails are lean and bring protein, iron and magnesium; the butter makes this a rich starter.

ingredients.name: Burgundy snails, prepared, with their shells

instructions: Beat the soft butter with the garlic, shallot, parsley, salt, pepper and white wine until evenly green.
Push a little butter into each shell, slip in a snail and seal the opening with more butter.
Stand the shells, opening up, in snail dishes or on a tray of coarse salt so they do not tip, and chill 15 to 30 minutes to firm the butter.
Bake at 400°F to 465°F (200°C to 240°C) for 8 to 12 minutes, until the butter bubbles and just browns.
Serve at once with the baguette for the butter.

citations.source: Le Bonbon Dijon, Escargots de Bourgogne, la tradition

recipes.curationNote: Le Bonbon: 4 dozen snails, 125 g demi-sel butter, 3 garlic, a bunch of parsley, pepper, 240°C 8 min. FrenchEntrée: 80 to 100 snails, 500 g butter, 300 g parsley, tarragon, garlic, spring onion, 2 tbsp white wine, 180°C 10 to 15 min. Kept about 50 g butter per dozen, between the two, with the small shallot and wine; tarragon left out as most Burgundian versions do. Snails are not in the food database.

recipes.name: Jambon Persillé
recipes.flavorProfile: Pink flakes of ham set in a clear, white wine jelly marbled bright green with parsley and garlic, cool and sharp with vinegar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean ham gives protein, and the parsley adds vitamin K and vitamin C; it is cured pork, so it is salty.

ingredients.name: lightly salted pork shoulder (palette demi-sel) or ham hock
ingredients.cutPrep: soaked 30 minutes to 2 hours to remove salt
2 whole cloves stuck in the onion
20 g whole for the broth, 15 g finely chopped

instructions: Soak the pork in cold water for 30 minutes to 2 hours (longer for a saltier piece), then drain.
Put it in a large pot with the white wine, water, onion with cloves, carrot, leek, the whole garlic, peppercorns, bay and thyme. Bring to a boil and skim.
Simmer gently for 2 hours 30 minutes to 4 hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Lift out the meat. Strain the broth, boil it to reduce by half, stir in the vinegar and the soaked gelatine, and leave it to cool until it begins to thicken.
Flake the meat, removing skin and gristle, and mix it with the mustard, the chopped garlic and most of the parsley.
Pack the meat into a terrine or bowl in layers, scattering parsley between them, and pour the cool broth over to cover.
Chill for 12 to 24 hours until set, then slice and serve with cornichons and bread.

citations.source: Le Bonbon Dijon, Comment faire un jambon persillé
Stefan Gourmet, Jambon persillé (ham hock terrine)

recipes.curationNote: Le Bonbon: 2.5 kg palette demi-sel soaked 30 min, white Burgundy, wine vinegar, onion with clove, carrot, peppercorns, bay, simmer 4 h, broth reduced by half, 20 g gelatine, flaked with garlic and parsley, set 12 h or more. Stefan Gourmet: ham hocks, aligoté, leek, carrot, onion with cloves, white wine vinegar, Dijon, parsley, 2 to 3 h, reduced to 1 L, set 24 h. Lightly salted pork is not in the food database.

recipes.name: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep, sweet onions slowly browned in butter, a dark beefy broth with a splash of white wine, and a lid of toasted bread under bubbling, browned Gruyère.
recipes.healthBenefit: Onions bring fibre and plant compounds and the cheese brings protein and calcium, though the cheese lid makes this a rich, salty bowl.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: a few sprigs, in the bouquet garni
cut in 1 cm slices, dried in the oven

instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat, add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring often, for 40 to 60 minutes, until they are soft and an even deep golden brown.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 2 to 3 minutes so it cooks without burning.
Pour in the white wine and scrape up the brown bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add the hot brown veal stock and chicken stock, the thyme and the bay leaf, bring to a simmer and cook gently for 20 to 30 minutes.
Meanwhile dry the baguette slices in the oven at 350°F (180°C) for 8 to 10 minutes, until crisp.
Remove the thyme and bay, season with salt, pepper and a little nutmeg.
Heat the broiler to 475°F (250°C). Ladle the soup into 6 ovenproof bowls set on a baking sheet.
Lay the toasted bread on top, cover thickly with the Gruyère and broil for 5 to 8 minutes, until the cheese bubbles and browns. Serve at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the Gruyère melted over the top.
From the cheese and the long-simmered stocks.

citations.source: 750g, Soupe à l'oignon gratinée comme dans les bistrots parisiens
Qui veut du fromage, Soupe à l'oignon gratinée au fromage

recipes.name: Vichyssoise
recipes.region: Bourbonnais (Vichy), as written by Louis Diat
recipes.flavorProfile: Cold, silky and pale, with the gentle sweetness of leeks, the body of potato and fresh chives on top.
recipes.healthBenefit: Leeks and potatoes bring potassium, vitamin C and some fibre, while the cream makes it a rich soup best served in a modest cup.

ingredients.cutPrep: white part, washed and thinly sliced
floury potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Melt the butter in a pot over low heat, add the leeks and onion and soften them for 10 to 15 minutes, without letting them color.
Add the potatoes, the water and the salt, bring to a boil and simmer for 15 to 25 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart.
Pour in the milk and bring back just to a simmer.
Blend until completely smooth, then pass through a fine sieve.
Stir in 200 ml of the cream, season with white pepper and taste for salt.
Cool, then chill for at least 3 to 4 hours, until very cold.
Serve in chilled cups with a spoonful of the remaining cream on each and the chives scattered over.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the potatoes, partly kept in the cooking liquid that stays in the soup.

citations.source: RTBF, Vichyssoise et roulade de sole

Wikipedia gives Louis Diat's account, after his mother's leek and potato soup near Vichy, finished with milk and cream and served cold with chives; both are kept.

recipes.name: Potage Parmentier
recipes.flavorProfile: A smooth, comforting leek and potato soup, buttery and mild, with crisp croutons and a fresh lift of chervil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Potatoes and leeks give potassium, vitamin C and some fibre, in a soup that is filling without being heavy.

ingredients.cutPrep: floury potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks

instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium-low heat and soften the leeks for 8 to 10 minutes, without browning.
Add the potatoes, the stock and the water, bring to a boil and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the potatoes are very soft.
Blend until smooth (or pass through a food mill for the old texture).
Stir in the cream, warm through without boiling and season with salt and pepper.
Serve in bowls with the croutons and chopped chervil on top.
recipes.curationNote: Noovo Moi gives the quantities (butter, leek whites, a kilo of potatoes, poultry stock, cream). The 1869 Journal des demoiselles definition quoted by La langue française gives the classic finish of chervil and fried croutons, so both are kept.

recipes.name: Bouillabaisse

recipes.healthBenefit: The fish make it high in protein with selenium, iodine and vitamin B12, and the soup is built on olive oil and vegetables, with the rouille adding most of the fat.

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat, add the onion, leek, garlic, tomatoes, fennel, parsley, thyme, bay, orange zest and half the saffron, and cook for 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the soup fish and cook, stirring, for 15 minutes, until they break down to a paste.
Pour in the boiling water, salt lightly and keep it at a strong boil for 30 minutes to 1 hour so the oil and broth bind.
Pass everything through a food mill, then through a fine sieve, pressing hard, and return the broth to the cleaned pot with the rest of the saffron.

Make the rouille: pound the garlic to a paste with a pinch of salt, add the squeezed bread crumb, the yolk, the cayenne and a pinch of saffron, then work in the 200 ml of olive oil drop by drop, as for a mayonnaise.
Bring the broth back to a boil, add the potatoes and the firm fish (conger, monkfish and scorpion fish) and cook for 10 to 15 minutes.
Add the delicate fish (John Dory and gurnard) and cook for 5 to 10 minutes more, until all the fish is just cooked and the potatoes are tender. Taste for salt and pepper.
Serve the broth first in hot plates over the garlic toasts with the rouille, then bring the fish and potatoes to the table on a warm platter, moistened with broth.

recipes.name: Bisque de Homard
recipes.flavorProfile: Velvety, coral-colored and deeply savory, with roasted lobster shell, cognac and tomato behind a little cream and a warm pinch of cayenne.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lobster brings protein, zinc, copper and selenium, while the cream and cognac make this a rich, special-occasion soup.
instructions: Split the lobster lengthwise from the head, remove the gravel sac and chop the head and shell into pieces; keep the tail and claws aside.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over high heat and sear the shell pieces for 3 to 5 minutes, until bright red, then add the tail and claws for 2 to 3 minutes and lift them out.
Add the butter, carrot, celery and shallot and sweat over low heat for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then pour in the cognac and let it reduce (or flame it carefully).
Add the white wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, garlic, tarragon, rice, fish stock and water.
Simmer gently, covered, for 35 to 40 minutes.
Meanwhile pick the meat from the tail and claws and cut it in small pieces; put the emptied shells back in the pot.
Blend the bisque with the shells in short bursts, then pass it through a fine sieve, pressing hard to get all the flavor.
Reheat gently, stir in the crème fraîche, season with salt and a pinch of cayenne, and serve with the lobster meat and small croutons.

recipes.name: Pâte à Galettes (Buckwheat Galette Batter)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thin, lacy, earthy pancake with a nutty, slightly bitter buckwheat taste and crisp brown edges.

instructions: Put the buckwheat flour and salt in a bowl and make a well in the middle.
Break in the egg and pour in about a third of the water, then beat hard with a whisk or your hand for 3 to 5 minutes to give the batter body.
Beat in the rest of the water a little at a time until the batter is smooth and as thin as single cream.
Cover and rest it in the fridge for at least 2 hours, or overnight; stir it well before using and thin it with a spoonful of water if it has thickened.
Heat a crêpe pan or a flat griddle until very hot, wipe it with butter, pour in a small ladle of batter and tilt or spread it thin in one move.
Cook 1 to 2 minutes until the edges lift and brown, then turn it for 30 seconds to 1 minute, or fill it on the pan without turning.
